subject: Renewal discussion: run-rate reshuffle, credits & SLA carveouts
messages:
From: Asha Patel <asha@panterra.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@panterra.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal planning — Q4 term/credits discussion

David — thanks again for the run-through last week. We’re coming up on our contract renewal and I wanted to put a couple of constraints on the table so we can make progress on terms: 

- We need a predictable run-rate for forecasting; top priority is a price hold for the first 9 months of the renewal.
- We’re open to committing additional GPU hours, but commits must map to quarterly budgets (we cannot do big annual pre-pays).
- Any credits for overage or surge must be applied as invoice credits (not lender-style escrow).

Can you share an approach that balances a price hold + quarterly-structured commits? Rajiv is included for finance alignment.

Best,
Asha Patel
Head of Platform Ops, Panterra Systems
asha@panterra.com
+1 415-555-0198
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Patel <asha@panterra.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — Q4 term/credits discussion

Asha — really appreciate the clarity. I spoke with Finance and Product about three possible structures that meet Panterra’s constraints; high level here and I attached a draft term sheet for the one we think balances predictability and operational flexibility (panterra_term_sheet_v1.pdf). Key points: 

1) Staggered run-rate + price guard
   - We can offer a 9-month price hold on per-token rates for the primary model family you use, provided you commit to a quarterly minimum (Q1/Q2/Q3 at X tokens each). If you underuse, we convert shortfall to future credit (applied as invoice credit).

2) Quarterly-structured commit (no single annual pre-pay)
   - Commitments are set per quarter; leftover unused commitment in a quarter becomes a flexible credit pool for the next quarter (6-month expiry). This preserves your budget cadence.

3) Surge protection credits (invoice application)
   - Instead of escrow, we’ll issue surge credits when you exceed committed throughput beyond a threshold. Credits appear as line-item invoice credits within the next billing cycle.

4) SLA carveout option
   - For a 6-month trial of a higher uptime SLA (99.9 -> 99.95) we can include an SLA carveout that limits rollback liability; after the trial we revert to standard SLA unless mutually renewed.

Operational asks from our side: we’d like access to a stable usage export each Friday (CSV stub suggested) so our cost-engineers can confirm commit burn rate and activate credits automatically. I’ve looped in Monica from CS to draft the runbook for weekly usage export and credit automation.

If this looks acceptable we’ll iterate the term sheet and runbook. Proposed next step: 30-minute call Wednesday 10am PT to align finance + ops.

Thanks — I’ve attached the draft term sheet (panterra_term_sheet_v1.pdf) and last quarter usage (panterra_q2_usage_summary.csv) for context.

— David Kim
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
david.kim@redwood.ai | +1 650-555-0123

Attachment: panterra_term_sheet_v1.pdf (draft)
Attachment: panterra_q2_usage_summary.csv (summary)
From: Asha Patel <asha@panterra.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@panterra.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 08:49:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — Q4 term/credits discussion

David — thank you, this is helpful. A few clarifying items from our side after reviewing the term sheet: 

- Price hold: We can accept a 9-month price hold only if the quarterly minimums are set conservatively. Can you model a lower-commit threshold for Q1 and larger step-ups in Q2/Q3?
- Credits: Invoice credits are fine, but we need a reporting proof (signed CSV export) when a credit is applied. That reporting must include token-level breakdown by route/model.
- SLA carveout: We want the SLA trial but need a rollback protection clause — if uptime drops below 99.5% during the trial we want an automatic credit equal to one month’s average spend.

Operationally, Rajiv wants to understand how the flexible credit pool behaves in a quarter where we spike and then drop. Example: if we spike 2x in week 2 and fall to 0.5x in week 8, how does credit expiration and re-allocation work? Can Monica outline the automation that would reconcile spikes to credits?

If acceptable, we’ll confirm the 30-minute call for Wednesday 10am PT.

— Asha
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Patel <asha@panterra.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Rajiv Menon <rajiv@panterra.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2026 15:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — Q4 term/credits discussion

Asha / Rajiv — thanks for the precise asks. Quick answers and next steps before the call: 

- Lower Q1 commit option: yes — we’ll produce two modeled ladders in the updated term sheet (conservative Q1 / stepped Q2-Q3). I asked Marissa to price both ladders; Ben is on pricing sensitivity for surge thresholds.

- Credit reporting: Monica will draft the exported CSV spec (route/model, token counts, timestamp, credit applied, trigger reason) and we’ll include a signed hash on every weekly export for auditability.

- SLA rollback protection: we can include an automatic remedial credit equal to 1x of the monthly average spend if uptime < 99.5% during the trial window. Legal will formalize the language in the next iteration.

- Flexible credit behavior on spikes: Monica — see above; plan is: (a) credits originate from unused committed units or surge-trigger credits, (b) credits are applied first against the subsequent quarter’s invoices, (c) credits from a quarter expire after 6 months, (d) when a spike occurs within a quarter we apply surge credits within the next invoice and reconcile against the weekly signed exports. I’ll ask Monica to attach a short runbook before our call.

Next step: we’ll circulate an updated term sheet and a 2-page runbook by EOD tomorrow. Confirming call Wed 10am PT — invitation to follow. Thanks all for moving quickly.

— David

On the call: David (Redwood), Monica (Redwood), Marissa (Redwood pricing), Ben (Redwood pricing ops), Asha (Panterra), Rajiv (Panterra finance).
